reference.one_line: 29-year-old teacher, day 7 for mania after stopping lithium; mania largely settled, now lithium toxicity (level 1.6) with kidney injury from dehydration and ibuprofen.

handoff.summary: Ysolde Tiverton-Mbali, 29, a voluntary patient since 14 Nov, has bipolar I disorder; her manic episode with psychotic features has largely resolved on lithium and olanzapine 15 mg. This morning the lithium level was 1.6 with coarse tremor, unsteadiness, slightly slurred speech, nausea and loose stools; creatinine is 1.2 (baseline 0.7), sodium 146 and standing pressure 88/54. Lithium has been held since 08:00 and sodium chloride 0.9% runs at 150 mL/h. Ibuprofen 600 mg, eight doses since 14 Nov, is still active with a dose due at 14:00 although the medicine consult said to stop it. Sleep has slipped to 4.5 and 3.5 hours; she has no thoughts of self-harm, and the 15-minute checks are for fall risk.
to_do: Do not give the 14:00 ibuprofen; get the order discontinued; acetaminophen if cramps return
Lithium level and chemistry at 16:00 and 06:00; keep the 20:00 lithium on hold
Fluid chart: aim for urine above 100 mL/h; lying and standing pressure each shift; help her to the bathroom
Continue olanzapine 15 mg and the sleep chart; correct the note (sleep 4.5 and 3.5 hours; 16 Nov level was post-dose)
if_then: If the level reaches 2.0, or she becomes confused, develops jerks or a seizure, or urine output falls, then call medicine and transfer to a medical bed
If sodium rises above 146, then ask medicine to review the fluid
If elated mood, pressured speech or a night under 3 hours returns while lithium is held, then call psychiatry; lorazepam or olanzapine as needed, never haloperidol
If she asks to leave, then remember she is voluntary and has capacity: explain the risk of a high level, call the resident, and reassess

reference.brief_hospital_course: Ms Tiverton-Mbali, 29, a music teacher with bipolar I disorder, was brought in by her sister on 11 Nov after four nights almost without sleep, heavy spending and grandiose and persecutory beliefs, five weeks after stopping lithium and olanzapine because of 7 kg weight gain. She was admitted under an emergency hold on constant observation; lithium 600 mg twice daily and olanzapine (increased to 15 mg) were restarted and she accepted all treatment. Capacity to consent to treatment was confirmed on 13 Nov and she became a voluntary patient on 14 Nov. Mood, sleep and thinking improved steadily and a family meeting was held on 16 Nov. On 14 Nov scheduled ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours was ordered for period pain. From 15 Nov she developed tremor, falling fluid intake and loose stools. A level of 1.8 mmol/L on 16 Nov was drawn 90 minutes after a dose and treatment continued; a true 12-hour level on 17 Nov was 1.6 with creatinine 1.2 mg/dL (baseline 0.7), sodium 146 and a postural drop. Lithium was held, intravenous saline started and general medicine consulted, who diagnosed mild to moderate toxicity from dehydration and ibuprofen and advised stopping ibuprofen. Discharge moved to 20 to 22 Nov.

Medicine review this evening; fluid rate
When and at what dose to restart lithium

qa.a: Haloperidol: acute neck muscle spasm (dystonia) in 2025.
Voluntary since she signed in at 10:15 on 14 Nov; the emergency hold began 04:30 on 11 Nov.

qa.q: What were the lying and standing blood pressures this morning?
qa.a: 102/62 lying and 88/54 standing with dizziness; pulse 106.

qa.q: How have the lithium levels run?
qa.a: 0.1 on admission, 0.7 on 14 Nov, 1.8 on 16 Nov (drawn 90 minutes after a dose, so not comparable), 1.6 on 17 Nov as a true 12-hour level.
Creatinine 0.7, 0.7, 1.0, 1.2; filtration rate 119 to 62; urea nitrogen 11 to 26; sodium 139 to 146.

qa.q: What does the sleep chart show?
qa.a: 1.5, 2.5, 4 and 5.5 hours on the mornings of 12 to 15 Nov, then 4.5 on 16 Nov and 3.5 on 17 Nov: improving, then worse.

qa.q: How many ibuprofen doses has she had, and over what period?
qa.a: Eight doses of 600 mg, from 22:15 on 14 Nov to 06:00 on 17 Nov; another is charted as due at 14:00.
20:00 on 15 Nov (new fine tremor), about 22 hours after the first ibuprofen and about 36 hours before lithium was held.
The level is 1.6 with mild to moderate signs and she is passing urine; fluids and stopping the causes should clear it. Transfer is advised at 2.0, confusion, jerks, seizure or falling urine.

qa.q: Why was observation raised to every 15 minutes?
qa.a: Fall risk from unsteadiness and dizziness on standing, not risk to herself.

qa.q: Was her capacity to decide about leaving reassessed on 14 Nov before she signed in voluntarily?
qa.a: The chart does not say. The attending asked for reassessment that morning; only the signing at 10:15 is recorded.

qa.q: Who reduced observation to every 30 minutes on 15 Nov, and why?
qa.a: Not documented. The flowsheet shows the change from 20:00 on 15 Nov; there is no order or note explaining it.

tasks.prompt: Review the active medication orders for interactions and against the consultants' recommendations.
expected_findings: Ibuprofen 600 mg every 8 hours ordered 14 Nov 21:50; eight doses given while lithium rose from 0.7 to 1.6
Anti-inflammatory drugs reduce lithium clearance; her home list said to avoid it and acetaminophen was available
Medicine said at 11:10 to stop it, yet the order is active with a dose due 14:00
acceptable_actions: Withhold the 14:00 dose and discontinue the order
Use acetaminophen; remove ibuprofen from the discharge list and teach her and her sister
must_not: Restart lithium, or add a diuretic

tasks.prompt: Check that the lithium levels were collected as ordered and can be compared with one another.
expected_findings: Order: sample 12 hours after the evening dose and before the morning dose
On 16 Nov lithium was given at 08:10 and blood drawn at 09:40: a near-peak value of 1.8
It cannot be compared with the 12-hour levels 0.7 and 1.6; the fall from 1.8 to 1.6 is not real, and the day 6 note wrongly called it 'still settling' and continued the dose
acceptable_actions: Label the 16 Nov result as post-dose
Ensure future levels are true 12-hour samples
must_not: Say the level is already falling

tasks.prompt: Compare today's psychiatry progress note with the nursing sleep record.
expected_findings: Note: 'about 6 hours on each of the last two nights'
Sleep chart: 4.5 and 3.5 hours; the night nursing note agrees
Sleep is worsening, which matters for relapse and as a sign she is unwell
acceptable_actions: Correct the note and tell the team
evidence: notes: progress note 17 Nov 09:00; night nursing note

tasks.prompt: Establish when signs of lithium toxicity first appeared and what preceded them.
expected_findings: Progress note calls the tremor 'new this morning' (17 Nov)
Flowsheet: new fine tremor at 20:00 on 15 Nov, about 22 hours after the first ibuprofen; intake falling from that day, loose stools from 16 Nov; shaky hands noted at the family meeting
Cause is ibuprofen plus dehydration, and signs were present about 36 hours before lithium was held
acceptable_actions: Correct the timeline and the stated cause
Use it for teaching and incident review
must_not: Attribute toxicity to poor drinking alone
evidence: notes: night nursing note; family meeting

tasks.prompt: Review today's medication administration record for doses not given.
expected_findings: Lithium 08:00 is marked held and 20:00 is on hold
This was deliberate, for a level of 1.6 with tremor, as the progress note and medicine consult direct
Giving it would be the error
acceptable_actions: Confirm the hold is appropriate and continue it until review
must_not: Give the held or the 20:00 dose

epilogue.note: What happens AFTER 'now' in this simulated world. Never shown in the chart; for outcome-prediction ground truth.
epilogue.course: At 14:40 her nurse, having read the medicine consult, withheld the ibuprofen and paged the resident, who discontinued it. The 16:00 level was 1.3 with creatinine 1.1 and sodium 147; medicine changed the drip to half-strength saline and pushed oral water. By the next morning the level was 0.9 and the tremor fine; the drip came down that afternoon. Off lithium she slept four hours on 19 Nov and was more talkative, which settled with olanzapine and one dose of lorazepam. With creatinine 0.7 on 20 Nov, lithium restarted at 450 mg twice daily; the 12-hour level on 24 Nov was 0.7. She went home to her sister on 25 Nov with a written sick-day rule and a card saying no anti-inflammatory painkillers.

events.event: Ibuprofen withheld by nurse and discontinued by resident
Medicine review: fluid changed to sodium chloride 0.45% at 125 mL/h, oral water encouraged
Lithium 0.9, creatinine 0.9, sodium 143; intravenous fluid stopped 14:00
Slept 4 hours, more talkative; olanzapine continued, lorazepam once
Lithium restarted at 450 mg twice daily (creatinine 0.7 that morning)
Clinic review: mood stable, lithium 0.7, sleeping 7 hours

outcomes_30_day.notable: Held lithium correctly during a stomach bug on 10 Dec (level 0.8 next day); mood stable, returning to school on 4 Jan.

portal_messages.subject: olanzapine - can't keep doing this
portal_messages.body: Hi, I know we said we'd talk about switching at my next visit but that's not till the end of October. None of my concert clothes fit. Seven kilos. I've been well for a year and a half and honestly I feel cured, and I'm starting to think I'd rather just stop the olanzapine myself than wait five more weeks. Is there any way to be seen sooner? Ysolde
ideal_reply_points: She is telling you she may stop treatment: call within a day and bring the appointment forward
Take the weight seriously; offer a switch plan and dietitian now
Explain relapse risk if stopped suddenly; ask her not to stop lithium

portal_messages.subject: Ysolde after today's meeting
portal_messages.body: It's Oriel. Thank you for today, it was so good to see her like herself. But after you left she couldn't get her tea to her mouth without spilling, and she said she felt sick and a bit off. Her hands weren't like that on Saturday. Is that the tablets? She also said she's hardly drinking because water tastes funny. Mum is fretting. Could someone look at her tonight?
ideal_reply_points: New tremor, nausea and poor drinking on lithium need review tonight, with a level and kidney test
Check what else has been started (painkillers)
Thank her; relatives often notice first

portal_messages.subject: period due - what can I actually take?
portal_messages.body: Home ten days and doing okay, sleeping, Oriel is being a dragon about the evening tablets. My period is due next week and the first two days are always grim. I've got the card that says no ibuprofen. Does that mean nothing at all? What about the one you rub on, or naproxen? I'd rather ask than end up back on a drip.
ideal_reply_points: Acetaminophen regularly, heat pad, gentle movement
No ibuprofen, naproxen or aspirin-type tablets; ask before using gels
Keep drinking; the pill can be reviewed if cramps stay bad

portal_messages.subject: sick all night - take lithium?
portal_messages.body: I've been up since 2 with vomiting and the runs, I think it's the bug going round Oriel's office. I've kept down maybe half a glass of water. My sheet says something about sick days but Oriel has it at work. Do I take this morning's lithium or not? Hands are a bit trembly but that might just be no sleep.
ideal_reply_points: Do not take lithium while vomiting or with diarrhoea
Small sips often; blood test for level and kidney function today or tomorrow
Emergency department if confused, very unsteady, coarse tremor or unable to keep fluid down

portal_messages.subject: Re: sick all night - take lithium?
portal_messages.body: Morning Ysolde, well done for checking. Don't take lithium this morning, or tonight if you are still being sick. Small sips of water or rehydration drink every few minutes. Take your olanzapine tonight if it will stay down. I've booked a blood test at the clinic for 9:00 tomorrow. If the shaking gets worse, you feel muddled or can't keep anything down by this afternoon, go to the emergency department and show them your card.

conversation.setting: Family meeting in the quiet room, Behavioural Health, 16 Nov 15:00; mother joining by video

turns.speaker: P. Sorensen-Adu
turns.text: Mrs Tiverton-Mbali, can you see and hear us? Good. Ysolde, you asked for this meeting, so would you like to start?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay. Um. I want to say what happened, myself. I stopped my tablets. Start of October.

turns.speaker: mother
turns.text: Both of them?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Both, Mama. I'd put on seven kilos and I felt... cured. I thought I didn't need them.

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: And for a week or two she seemed fine. Then she stopped sleeping. I'd get up and she'd be planning lessons at three in the morning.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They were good lessons.

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: Some of them. Then the parcels started. And then the mission.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: Ysolde, how do you think about the mission today?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm embarrassed. I'm not sure it was real. Probably it was the illness.

turns.speaker: mother
turns.text: She sounds like my daughter again. Last week on the phone I didn't know her.

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: She's back. That's what I keep saying.

turns.speaker: mother
turns.text: But doctor, these tablets. Is it for life? She's twenty-nine.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: I understand why that's frightening. Bipolar disorder is a long-term condition where mood swings very high or very low. Lithium is the best thing we have for keeping it steady, and for most people that means years. It's reviewed regularly, it's not a sentence.

turns.speaker: mother
turns.text: My sister takes it. She's had the blood tests for years.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: Then you know. The tests are because the helpful amount and the too-much amount are close together. It leaves through the kidneys, so drinking enough and normal salt in food matter.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two and a half litres. They keep telling me.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: They're right. Your level this morning was on the high side, so we're repeating it tomorrow before your dose.

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: And the weight? Because that's what'll make her stop again, if I'm honest.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Oriel.

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: It's true, though.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: It's a fair point. The weight is mostly the olanzapine. There are other medicines that do that job with less weight gain, and we'll plan a change properly instead of you having to choose between your health and your clothes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Then I want to stay on the lithium. And I want Oriel to keep the tablets for the first month.

turns.speaker: P. Sorensen-Adu
turns.text: Oriel, are you willing?

turns.speaker: sister
turns.text: Yes. What should I be watching for?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Me sleeping under five hours. Big ideas at night. Spending.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: That's exactly the list. Ysolde, are you all right? Your hand's shaking.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm tired. I feel a bit off today. It's been cramps and everything.

turns.speaker: Dr. Kowalczyk
turns.text: We'll keep an eye on that. So, to check we agree: lithium continues with blood tests, Oriel holds the medicines for a month, everyone knows the early signs, and we aim for home on the nineteenth if tomorrow's level is fine. Have I missed anything?

turns.speaker: mother
turns.text: No. Thank you for looking after her.

turns.speaker: P. Sorensen-Adu
turns.text: I'll write this up and give you each a copy of the warning signs.
